Notes on neural networks, starting with how a single layer computes its output
and building toward training with backpropagation.

## Topics in this module

- **[Forward Propagation & Activation Functions](forward-propagation/index.qmd)** —
  one fully connected layer as a graph and as a matrix ($\mathbf{a}_2 = W f(\mathbf{a}_1)$),
  the common activation functions, and softmax for classification. Comes with a
  [NumPy notebook](forward-propagation/demo.ipynb) that draws the layer in 2D and 3D
  and plots every activation with its derivative.
- **[Depth, Width, and Activation — A Controlled Study](architecture-study/index.ipynb)** —
  changing one factor at a time to see how it shapes a network's output, first with
  random (untrained) weights and then after training on the same curve.
- **[What Do the Weights Mean?](weights-study/index.ipynb)** — reading a layer's
  weight matrix: hidden nodes as boundary pieces for 2D classification, and as
  templates for images built from known strokes — and when that intuition breaks down.
- **[Backpropagation](backpropagation/index.qmd)** — deriving the gradient of the
  loss with respect to every weight of a 4-5-3-2 network: the output layer one
  weight at a time, then the delta recursion
  $\delta^{[l]} = (W^{[l+1]})^T \delta^{[l+1]} \odot f'^{[l]}(a^{[l]})$ and
  $\partial L / \partial W^{[l]} = \delta^{[l]} (x^{[l-1]})^T$. Comes with a
  [NumPy notebook](backpropagation/demo.ipynb) that checks the gradients against
  finite differences and trains the network, with and without biases.
- *Training in practice (initialization, optimizers, regularization)* — planned.
